MARKET.head: Vinitaly.USA moves to New York's Pier 36 for October 2026 debut
MARKET.summ: The Italian wine trade event makes its New York City debut October 26 and 27, bringing 300 exhibitors and 2,500 wines to Pier 36
takeaways: Vinitaly.USA makes its first New York City appearance at Pier 36 on October 26 and 27, 2026, after two years in Chicago.
The fair will host 300 exhibitors presenting 2,500 labels, its largest exhibitor count to date, including Asti DOCG, Sicilia DOC and Prosecco DOC.
Registration is open, and the event features a 95-winery delegation organized by the Italian Trade Agency plus the wine2wine Vinitaly Business Forum.

MARKET.head: Restaurant beverage directors adapt to rising costs and wholesaler collapse
MARKET.summ: It’s a hard time to run a beverage program. Costs are escalating due in part to an unhappy blend of tariffs, supply chain issues, and general inflation. The wholesale sector of the drinks industry is in a tremendous amount of flux following the collapse of Republic National Distributing Company (RNDC) over the last year,...
takeaways: Wholesaler RNDC collapsed from second-largest US beverage distributor to Chapter 11 bankruptcy in under two years.
Will Jones of The Hope Farm and Little Bird in Fairhope, Ala. now substitutes Burgundy villages for Premier Cru because prices rose sharply.
Felipe de Assis Villela of Bluepoint Hospitality Group in Easton, Md. says he avoids restaurant markups of 200-300 percent.

MARKET.head: Clase Azul and Patrón lead list of world's most expensive tequilas
MARKET.summ: Though many consumers might recognize tequila as what they encountered in a shot in college or as the ingredient in their favorite cocktail, there’s also a market for extremely high-end tequila. These luxury bottles, often from prestigious brands like Clase Azul and Patrón, are revered for both their flavor profiles and...
takeaways: Wine Searcher ranked the world's ten most expensive tequilas, mostly from Clase Azul and Patrón.
Many of the priciest bottlings come from limited runs of under 500 bottles, with some as few as 299 or 300.
Packaging includes artisanal decanters made with artists, such as clay decanters with sterling silver and crystal decanters.

MARKET.head: Seven proposed US AVAs spanning California, Oregon, New Jersey and New York await approval
MARKET.summ: From Minnesota to New Jersey, seven proposed AVAs aim to distinguish emerging regions by climate, soils, and grape varieties
takeaways: Seven potential new American Viticultural Areas are in early stages, each needing years of review by the federal TTB.
The proposed Deschutes River AVA would be central Oregon's first recognized winegrowing region, spanning 723,760 acres.
The proposed Hunterdon Hills AVA in New Jersey covers about 200,000 acres, ranking second for suitable premier grape land.

MARKET.head: Cruise lines emerge as wine marketing channel for wineries seeking loyalty
MARKET.summ: From dedicated charters to custom bottlings, wineries are leveraging cruise partnerships to capture engaged audiences and drive long-term sales
takeaways: Cooper's Hawk chartered Virgin Voyages' Valiant Lady for a four-night Caribbean wine club cruise, and a second charter in February 2027 drew over 30% sign-ups.
Holland America launched a Columbia Valley brut fleetwide in 2024 with Four Feathers Wine Services, now its most-served adult beverage.
Eleven Eleven Wines reported a 33% conversion rate among non-club passengers after a seven-day Mediterranean sailing on Scenic Eclipse II.

MARKET.head: VinePair's weekly roundup lists Southern Glazer's probe and new spirits releases
MARKET.summ: This is VinePair’s Booze News Weekly Roundup, where we gather the hottest headlines and product releases every Friday for a snapshot of what’s happening in the beverage alcohol industry. It was a quiet week on the news front, but as we gear up for gifting season, there are a ton of new product drops.
takeaways: California has launched an investigation into Southern Glazer's over a reported bribery issue.
Trump is set to lift the tariff on Irish whiskey, per the roundup's headlines.
The roundup also covers GunBun's bankruptcy filing and a legal dispute between Stateside and AB InBev.

MARKET.head: Constellation Brands buys SpikedAde, a boozy sports drink brand, for $75 million
MARKET.summ: On Tuesday Constellation Brands announced its acquisition of SpikedAde, one of the leading ready-to-drink (RTD) beverages in the growing boozy sports drink segment. Constellation agreed to a payment of $75 million for 100 percent ownership of the fast-growing brand, though payments in the next five years could reach up to an...
takeaways: Constellation Brands agreed to pay $75 million for 100 percent ownership of SpikedAde, a vodka-based ready-to-drink brand.
Up to an additional $278 million could be paid over five years, contingent on the brand's performance.
The deal is Constellation's first move into hard sports drinks, a segment whose 'Ade' products passed one million cases this year.

CULTURE.head: Bouvet-Ladubay marks 175 years as Saumur's largest sparkling producer
CULTURE.summ: Set your navigation southwest from Paris and follow your wine-loving heart to the Loire. There, along the curving river’s central stretch, you’ll find the country’s third-largest wine region: a verdant, chateau-studded valley where waves of vines give birth to grapes destined for an effervescent future.
takeaways: Bouvet-Ladubay, founded in Saumur in 1851 by Etienne Bouvet and Célestine Ladubay, is celebrating its 175th anniversary this year.
The house is described as the largest producer of méthode traditionnelle sparkling wine in Saumur, with cellars covering eight kilometres.
Its wines are exported to around 50 countries, and the Monmousseau family has run the house since 1908.

CULTURE.head: Bartenders say American drinkers abroad are curious, though they still favor vodka
CULTURE.summ: Over decades of regular trips to Europe, Regine Rousseau, the Chicago-based founder of wine marketing and events consultancy Shall We Wine, never really subscribed to the directive often preached by U.S. travel publications: When traveling abroad, try not to let your American show. “Number one: I like wearing really bright...
takeaways: European bartenders say American bar guests in 2026 are curious and open, though many still order vodka Martinis.
Connaught Bar in London makes about 30,000 Martinis a year, with many American guests specifying vodka over gin.
Americans abroad often request spirit substitutions like bourbon, and some ask for American drinks such as the Cosmopolitan.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Canadian Sparkling Wine: a rare tasting crossing the country, with 24 different wines
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Canadian Sparkling Wine is a category that is progressing nicely. This tasting was a selection of 24, across many different
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: A rare cross-country tasting of 24 Canadian sparkling wines was held in Niagara, which is over-represented as a result.
Trius Showcase Blanc de Blancs NV, from Niagara, was tasted and scored 93/100, while York Reserve 2016 from Niagara-on-the-Lake also scored 94/100.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Encyclopedia of Wine - Fresh Take or Same Same?
NEWSLETTERS.summ: I take a look at a brand new reference work to see how it stacks up with the competition
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Dorling Kindersley's The Encyclopedia of Wine publishes October 8 in the UK and November 10 in the US.
The book was written by 28 contributors, including Jane Anson on Bordeaux and Wink Lorch on the Jura.
It is a 400-page book, positioned against Oxford Companion to Wine and The World Atlas of Wine from the Robinson team.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Arizcuren, Rioja low & high
NEWSLETTERS.summ: When urban Logroño winery meets the wilds of the Mediterranean
NEWSLETTERS.author: Miquel Hudin
takeaways: Arizcuren, owned by Javier Arizcuren, is the most urban winery in Rioja, located in central Logroño, a city of 150,000 people.
The winery produces around 30,000 bottles a year from its small central space, which also houses Javier's architecture office.
Arizcuren sources grapes from hills south of Quel in Rioja Oriental, a Mediterranean-influenced area where Grenache is significant.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Red and White and Roero All Over
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Notes from my week in Piemonte, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Meg Maker returned from a four-day Roero tour, where Roero's soils are sedimentary sandstone rather than the marl found in the Langhe to the south.
Roero's D.O.C.G. grapes are white Arneis and red Nebbiolo; producers plant roughly 1,000 hectares of Arneis versus 360 hectares of Nebbiolo.
Maker says Roero Nebbiolo reds sell in the U.S. for $25 to $45, while whites rarely top $25 except the Riserva bottlings.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Meet Your Robo-Somm
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The year is 2029. First-world civilisation has adapted to mass surveillance. Waymos and Tesla Robotaxis chauffeur NPCs between work and their domicile.
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Tim Atkin tested CellarTracker and food-pairing AI programs and found they often recommend Champagne for everything and confuse rosé with red.
Atkin says the SommPal app, developed by Marc Lewin, ranks up to five wine pairings per menu item and explains each recommendation's logic.
Lewin says SommPal is meant to help novice drinkers where no expert sommelier is available, not to replace sommeliers.

NEWSLETTERS.head: What I Learned at a Conference on Drinking
NEWSLETTERS.summ: From the invention of moderation to the return of temperance
NEWSLETTERS.author: Felicity Carter
takeaways: Felicity Carter reports from Dublin on a conference about drinking, noting the city was cooler than the rest of Europe at end of June.
